full_text:
- the point of staking is to secure the chain
- the chain is currently secured by $86 billion
- the amount of ETH being staked is up only (https://t.co/9kzGx2Ibhy)
- entities are building their entire business models around this yield because they view it as risk-free return
- it's locking up ETH with questionable additional security to the chain
- the more ETH staked, the more ETH is issued, with questionable security add
- once you get to majority ETH staked, the base currency in defi becomes an LST because it's more liquid and generates passive yield
- staking is not risk-free even if it's portrayed that way
- liquidity tends to concentrate on the most readily available assets, so chances are that we converge mostly on one LST
- so now (majority ETH staked) the base currency in defi comes with systemic risk that people aren't even aware of
- LSTs argue vehemently against issuance reduction because it's their entire business model (and everybody holds the LST, so they agree)
- the LST DAO represents a majority of locked ETH so their governance is now is heavily influential on ETH governance
- people layer that "passive, risk-free" yield with other yield (see recent KelpDAO situation)
- someone enters the chain for the first time, they see they have to buy an LST to get a loan because it's got the deepest liquidity (deeper liquidity than raw ETH)
- some irresponsible yield scheme falls apart and affects all the LSTs and depegs
- random person who just wanted a defi loan is affected
- wtf
- are we any better than the irresponsible bankers bundling subprime mortgages, leveraging them, and exposing regular people to ridiculous risk because they were chasing yield at any cost?
- all of this could have been secured by a 10% staking ratio but we got fucking greedy about free yield
